question:
An approximately circular oil patch spreads over the surface of water. At an instant when its radius is $6\ \text{m}$, its area is increasing at $18\pi\ \text{m}^2/\text{min}$.

(a) Determine the instantaneous rate at which the radius is increasing.

(b) Find the rate of change of the circumference of the patch at that instant.

(c) If the rate found in part (a) remains constant for the next $2$ minutes, calculate the increase in the radius during this period.
explanation:
(a)
The area of the circular patch is
$$A=\pi r^2$$
Differentiating with respect to time,
$$\frac{dA}{dt}=2\pi r\frac{dr}{dt}$$
Substituting $\frac{dA}{dt}=18\pi$ and $r=6$,
$$18\pi=2\pi(6)\frac{dr}{dt}$$
Therefore,
$$\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{18\pi}{12\pi}=\frac{3}{2}\ \text{m/min}$$

(b)
The circumference is
$$C=2\pi r$$
Differentiating with respect to time,
$$\frac{dC}{dt}=2\pi\frac{dr}{dt}$$
$$\frac{dC}{dt}=2\pi\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=3\pi\ \text{m/min}$$

(c)
If the radius continues to increase at $\frac{3}{2}\ \text{m/min}$ for $2$ minutes, its increase is
$$\Delta r=\frac{3}{2}\times 2=3\ \text{m}$$

options.A:
(a) $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{3}{2}$ m/min
(b) $\frac{dC}{dt}=3\pi$ m/min
(c) Radius increases by $3$ m
options.B:
(a) $\frac{dr}{dt}=3$ m/min
(b) $\frac{dC}{dt}=6\pi$ m/min
(c) Radius increases by $6$ m
options.C:
(a) $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{3}{4}$ m/min
(b) $\frac{dC}{dt}=\frac{3\pi}{2}$ m/min
(c) Radius increases by $\frac{3}{2}$ m
options.D:
(a) $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{1}{2}$ m/min
(b) $\frac{dC}{dt}=\pi$ m/min
(c) Radius increases by $1$ m
